disputed: Whether the Apple exemption constitutes illegal favoritism or ordinary lobbying/policy responsiveness has not been the subject of a legal ruling - Sen. Warren's letter is a political accusation, not an adjudicated finding. The administration has not disputed that Cook's direct engagement led to the exemption, but has not characterized it as improper.

items: May 28, 2025: the US Court of International Trade unanimously ruled the IEEPA tariffs illegal. The Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit upheld that ruling on August 29, 2025.

February 20, 2026: the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 in Learning Resources Inc. v. Trump / V.O.S. Selections v. United States that IEEPA does not authorize the president to impose tariffs, holding that tariff power is 'clearly a branch of the taxing power' reserved for Congress under Article I. Chief Justice Roberts joined Sotomayor, Kagan, Gorsuch, Barrett, and Jackson in the majority; Thomas, Kavanaugh, and Alito dissented. (Tax Foundation (https://taxfoundation.org/blog/supreme-court-trump-tariffs-ruling/))

IEEPA tariffs officially terminated February 24, 2026. The government had collected an estimated $160 billion in IEEPA tariff revenue by the time of the ruling; the case was remanded to lower courts to sort out refunds to importers. (White & Case (https://www.whitecase.com/insight-alert/united-states-terminates-ieepa-based-tariffs-following-supreme-court-decision))

The ruling did not affect industry-specific Section 232 tariffs (steel, aluminum, autos, trucks), which remain in place and are separately estimated to raise $635 billion over the next decade. Trump announced replacement tariffs under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 the same day as the ruling. (Holland & Knight (https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/02/supreme-court-strikes-down-ieepa-tariffs))
sections.label: Legal outcome

items: The Tax Foundation estimates the tariffs increased taxes by an average of $1,000 per US household in 2025 and roughly $820-1,300 per household in 2026 even after the IEEPA ruling, as replacement tariffs took effect. (Tax Foundation (https://taxfoundation.org/research/all/federal/trump-tariffs-trade-war/))

A Federal Reserve Bank of New York study found approximately 90% of the roughly $175 billion generated by IEEPA tariffs was paid by domestic consumers and businesses, not foreign exporters. (Levy Economics Institute (https://www.levyinstitute.org/publications/the-us-supreme-court-rules-and-future-prospects-of-trumps-tariff-gambit/))

Despite the stated goal of rebalancing trade and reviving manufacturing, the US goods trade deficit reached $1.24 trillion in 2025 (up 2.1% from 2024), and manufacturing employment fell by 88,000 jobs from January to December 2025. (Levy Economics Institute (https://www.levyinstitute.org/publications/the-us-supreme-court-rules-and-future-prospects-of-trumps-tariff-gambit/))
sections.label: Economic cost

items: Trump publicly stated there would be no tariff exemptions. Despite this, on April 12, 2025, US Customs and Border Protection issued guidance exempting smartphones, computers, semiconductors, and other electronics from the reciprocal tariffs and the 125% China tariff rate. (Fortune (https://www.fortune.com/2025/04/12/trump-tariff-exemptions-smartphones-chips-computers-solar-cells-tv-displays-electronics/))

A Washington Post report found Apple CEO Tim Cook engaged directly with the Trump administration following the tariff announcement and secured this exemption, worth billions of dollars to Apple; Trump himself publicly confirmed on April 14, 2025 that the exemption was intended to help 'Tim Cook...and that whole business.' (Sen. Warren (https://www.warren.senate.gov/?p=28675); AppleInsider (https://appleinsider.com/articles/25/04/14/trump-confirms-he-reduced-tariffs-to-help-tim-cook))

Sen. Elizabeth Warren wrote to Cook directly, stating the exemption 'raise[s] fresh concerns about influence-peddling by huge, well-connected corporations, and their ability to gain special favors from President Trump,' and noted she had already raised concerns that Trump's trade policy was 'becoming a corrupt scheme to enrich administration officials and those loyal to them.' (Sen. Warren (https://www.warren.senate.gov/?p=28675))
sections.label: Access-based exemptions

summary: On April 2, 2025 ('Liberation Day'), Trump imposed sweeping 'reciprocal' tariffs of 10-50% on nearly every US trading partner, citing the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) - on top of earlier IEEPA tariffs targeting Canada, Mexico, and China over fentanyl. IEEPA does not explicitly mention tariffs; it grants power to 'regulate' imports during a declared national emergency.
title: Trump tariffs: legal overreach, economic cost, and access-based exemptions
